title: GTA 6’s Jason Can Live His Best Life By Drinking A Beer And Eating A Donut Simultaneously
description: Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 looks like it will have an impressive attention to detail, and that includes how one of the main characters, Jason, can drink a beer and eat a donut at the same time. Now that's living. Rockstar boss Rob Nelson geeked out to The Guardian about GTA 6's finer details, including this one. According to the report, Jason can "take bites of a donut with one hand while sipping a beer with the other." Drink up. It’s unclear whether this is under the player’s active control or it just happens. In any event, the report also mentioned how Rockstar paid close attention to "the way that Jason eats a hot dog." These are very important details. GTA 6 features a body-shaping system, so if Jason, or Lucia, drink a lot of beer and pound hot dogs and donuts, they'll likely gain weight. But that weight can then be transformed into muscle by hitting the gym and pumping out sets. Another example of Rockstar's attention to detail in GTA 6 is how Jason can buy a six-pack of beer, then start jogging, holding the beers in the crook of his arm. The game shows you the liquid sloshing around in the bottles as he runs. GTA 6's attention to detail is a little ridiculous, with Rockstar seemingly going all out to create little details that players may never even notice. GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. Preloading is underway now, but the game itself doesn't unlock until November 19 at midnight local time.

title: It’s Ogre For GTA 6, As Shrek 2 Remastered Gets A Huge Discount At Launch
description: Grand Theft Auto VI is already eyed as a Game of the Year contender, and with pre-order sales in the millions, there are very few that can rival it. Except, of course, our favorite prince-beating, Fiona-loving ogre, Shrek. Remastering a cult classic based on the best Shrek movie, Shrek 2 Remastered is exactly what you’d expect, and with a launch discount, it’s enough to say, “That’ll do, Callum, that’ll do.” I wouldn’t be surprised if GTA 6 pre-orders are hitting new lows after this, especially with Shrek 2 Remastered on sale, but this isn’t a joke—this is an absolute classic of a game, polished up for a new generation to fall in love with. It’s a blast with friends, delivering a co-op adventure that follows the events of one of the best animated movies of all time, and I do not say that lightly. Don’t joke about Shrek 2. Taking you from Shrek’s iconic swamp all the way to Fiona’s home in the Kingdom of Far, Far Away, Shrek 2 Remastered sees you playing as the lovable cast of fairytale misfits, with in-laws who are frustrated with Shrek’s very existence and a Fairy Godmother who is far too keen to pair her son, Prince Charming, with Fiona. You know the story by now, and the game faithfully recreates it, adding plenty of action and fun in between. Each level switches up the cast of characters, with each offering various ways to fight enemies or get through obstacles. And, of course, there’s a mixture of minigames to help keep things interesting as you explore Shrek’s world. As a bonus, the remaster includes a whole host of upgrades, from improved visuals to a newly added photo mode and the ability to unlock cheats in Cheat Mode, making it easier to defeat the bosses. Of course, it’s been a long time since the original, but at the time, GameSpot’s staff gave the console version of the game a 6.8/10 in Ryan Davis’ Shrek 2 review. Over two decades later, the adaptation is ready to make you laugh, smile, and cry once again. The latter is mainly due to the onions and the…

title: Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet Has Some Unexpected Anime Influences
description: After years of post-apocalyptic survival stories and archaeological adventures, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet looks like a fresh opportunity for Naughty Dog to showcase a new sci-fi universe. Visually, the game draws on '80s sci-fi movies with analog technology and ancient hardware like CD players, but you can also thank a genre-defining anime film for shaping Intergalactic's look and feel. In an interview with Patton Oswalt during the Comic Creators Block Party 2026, Naughty Dog director Neil Druckmann said that Akira inspired Intergalactic on multiple levels, alongside other big anime properties like Cowboy Bebop. "For Intergalactic, we actually took a lot of inspiration from anime. Akira--everybody loves Akira--just like the animation, the big ideas, the kind of philosophical sci-fi ideas within that," Druckmann said. "We took a lot of inspiration from anime, stylistic inspiration, how they approach the story. The big kind of philosophical questions and ideas. We really want to tackle that, and surprise players in interesting ways. By the time you get to the end of Akira, it just goes on this wild ride. And we want to take someone on a similar wild ride." Druckmann mentioned that he grew up with the laser-disc version of Akira, the landmark 1988 anime film directed by Katsuhiro Otomo. It's not hard to see that influence visually, as the protagonist Jordan A. Mun wears a jacket that looks like it was pilfered from the wardrobe of Akira lead Shotaro Kaneda, and her spaceship also looks like it was manufactured by the same company responsible for the hotheaded biker's iconic motorcycle--maybe we'll even see an Akira slide in the game. Philosophically, Akira covers a wide range of topics explored over the decades, with the film primarily centered on themes of human technological overreach, spiritual immaturity, and the cyclical nature of creation and destruction. Those ideas have been debated for decades, and Naughty Dog has proven adept at balancing heavy…

title: Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet Is Entering Its Final Stage Of Development, With More To Come In 2027
description: Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet developer Naughty Dog has been largely radio silent about its upcoming sci-fi game since it was first revealed in 2024, but it looks like 2027 will bring a lot more information. Speaking to Patton Oswalt during the Comic Creators Block Party 2026, director Neil Druckmann teased that the game is entering its "final stage" of production. "We've only teased it, so I can't talk too much about it," Druckmann said. "But we're kind of like at the last stages of production, where we can play it, and we're refining and polishing it, and I can't wait to show it to the world." Druckmann also said that after 20 years of relatively grounded games set on Earth, Intergalactic represented an opportunity for the studio to combine everything it learned from its biggest franchises into an experience that blends "cinematic" storytelling with deep gameplay. "Something we've been really hungry for is to go sci-fi. We used to have another game franchise, called Jak and Daxter. We wanted to take everything we learned from that franchise--which is sci-fi, fantasy, the kind of pulp-action adventure stuff we learned with Uncharted, the kind of serious drama we got from The Last of Us. It really is a combination of those three franchises, and we really wanted to expand our deep gameplay systems. Like, can we sustain the kind of cinematic storytelling we're used to doing, and go even deeper with gameplay systems?" So when will we actually get to see the game in action? "We're going to show a lot next year, Druckman said. "We're going to show gameplay, more of the story. I think we’re going to really surprise people with what they think the game is and what it actually is." Previously, reports said Naughty Dog has entered a period of crunch to get the game over the finish line. Focused on the protagonist Jordan A. Mun-- played by Tati Gabrielle --a bounty hunter who becomes stranded on a planet called Sempiria, this will be Naughty Dog's first new IP after two…

title: Marvel 1943: Rise Of Hydra Isn’t Canceled, But Don’t Get Too Excited
description: Amid multiple delays and radio silence, a rumor that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra had been canceled began circulating this week. Developer Skydance quickly said the game is on track and nearly done—but it might not be what you expect. According to Kotaku, executive producer Lu Gigliotti told Skydance employees that he had spoken with the studio's executive leadership team, and that the game had not been canceled. "They asked me to make sure you all hear that directly. There is no truth to these claims," Giglotti reportedly wrote in the Skydance Slack group. Kotaku added that the game is approaching its Alpha milestone and is "close to done," but after reportedly running significantly over budget, the vision for this project has been scaled back. Marvel 1943 was also originally envisioned as a Netflix game before it was announced for PC and consoles, but most of its action is apparently mapped to a single button, and it's "lacking significant interaction" during gameplay. Essentially, the game might be structurally similar to Quantic Dream's interactive stories like Detroit: Become Human, rather than a meaty brawler like Insomniac's Spider-Man games. "We're continuing development on it, but Amy and the team have big ambitions for the level of quality that they want to hit. They are a relatively small team considering the AAA quality that they're delivering,” senior executive Shawn Kittelsen said earlier this year about the game's lengthy development. "What you've seen in previous footage is what the game looks like, and we're making it with a fraction of the resources that you see on other AAA games of the same type, and really trying to push a new development model that's a lot more responsible and sustainable." First announced in 2022 and fully revealed in 2024, Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra drew attention for its good-looking graphics and a storyline featuring multiple characters, including Captain America and Black Panther. The new report comes in the wake of layoffs…

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns, Effective Immediately
description: Nvidia has announced that Jensen Huang has resigned as president and CEO of the company, effective immediately. Nvidia's current Chief Financial Officer, Colette Kress, will serve as interim CEO while keeping her CFO duties until a permanent replacement for Huang can be found. Harvey C. Jones, a longtime tech executive and investor, has been appointed as Nvidia's first-ever Chair of the Board, and the company says that operations, product plans, and customer commitments will continue without interruption. Nvidia's Q3 2017 financial results will still be reported on its scheduled date of November 17. Things began to look dire for Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang after it was revealed that he'd been involved in an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy. This week, news broke that he'd also taken part in a second affair with one of his executives. According to The New York Times, the Nvidia board of directors scheduled a meeting to discuss the situation, just days after launching an independent investigation into him. After the affair was first exposed, Nvidia quickly issued a statement saying that none of the company's secrets, or US state secrets, had been compromised. Huang also issued a letter to Nvidia employees, apologizing to his wife and children. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang With AI technology taking off in the last couple of years, Nvidia has become a major supplier of the crucial hardware components powering this boom. While the company is best known for its graphics cards, its fortunes have risen exponentially as it has focused more heavily on AI chips, with Huang becoming the face of the AI boom in the US. Huang is also Nvidia's founder, having started the company in 1993 and run its day-to-day operations for decades. With a 3.56% stake, he's also Nvidia's largest shareholder. His removal could have huge ramifications for the company, given how involved he was in running it and the reported lack of a succession plan. The revelation of a second affair has seen…

title: Grand Theft Auto Has Broken So Much Ground, What Else Can GTA 6 Do?
description: GTA has built a reputation over the years as not just AAA gaming at its peak, but a new revolution for the medium upon each game's launch. So it struck me how after watching the Extended Look at GTA 6 back in August, there was considerable chatter in my social circles claiming it looked like an Xbox 360 game. I don't think these comments should be taken literally, given that the footage we've seen shows such tremendous graphical fidelity and detail that it would have been impossible on hardware from two generations ago. But there's a kernel of truth when poring over each video snippet and trying to consider just what is meaningfully new or different to this time. Perhaps the best way to do this is to actually look back over GTA's history and consider the ways each installment did break new ground for the series, and whether there is still space for new foundations GTA 6 can lay, or merely build upon. Grand Theft Auto 3: A new dimension While the first GTA already garnered acclaim and controversy in equal measure for giving players the freedom to cause criminal anarchy, it was GTA 3's change from the original's top-down perspective to a full 3D open world that propelled it into blockbuster success. Some of that was also stoked by controversies over the many morally reprehensible acts the game allows you to do. Grand Theft Auto 3 But beyond the tabloid headlines, GTA 3 set the standard for open-world games as we know it: You had the freedom to roam Liberty City on foot or by car, whether it was following silent protagonist Claude's story of revenge against psychotic ex-girlfriend Catalina, going off the rails to unleash your own chaos to drive up your Wanted rating--knowing that even if you were wasted or busted by the cops, you'd soon be back on your feet ready to do it all over again --or just listening to NPC chatter or radio stations to soak up the atmosphere of this living, breathing city. GTA 6 can realize this formula with the highest modern polish, but its…

title: After being laid off by Microsoft, former Doom devs found new Smash TV-influenced FPS studio that isn't "subject to investor demands"
description: Back in July, Doom developers id Software laid off around a hundred people as part of wider Microsoft blood-letting. Now, a few of those devs have founded a new employee-owned studio, Hidden Horses. Their first project is Danger Pay, a single-player FPS influenced by ancient arcade blaster Smash TV (pictured) and dystopian movies such as deadly gameshow fable The Running Man – itself an influence on Smash TV. Hidden Horses have 20 id Software alumni on the books, including former lead VFX artist Todd Boyce, principal engine programmer Dustin Land, senior AI and gameplay engineer Daniel Young, producer Andrew Willis, senior technical designer Jordan Turner, principal technical designer Tim Locke, and senior skybox artist Allison Dombek. They're looking to make "the kind of old school shooters that we think people want more of," in Land's words. Read more

title: Steam’s Growing Review Backlog Has Cost Another Game Its Launch Date
description: Steam's growing backlog for approving game builds appears to be getting worse, as yet another studio's game is stuck in the purgatory of the platform's review program. Australia Did It: End-of-the-World Railway Defense Business, a post-apocalyptic game about keeping a cargo railway running after society has collapsed, was originally scheduled to launch on November 10, but it's stuck waiting for Steam's mandatory QA review before it can be published. "Unfortunately, we're stuck waiting for Steam to review and approve our launch build. We have been waiting for a few weeks now and sadly don't know when they will finally get around to it," Australia Did It publisher Mystic Forge wrote in an update. "We're hoping to be able to launch as soon as possible and will update all of you the second we get an update. We really appreciate all of your continued support and apologize for the situation. We can't wait for you to check out the final game and hope to be able to get it into your hands soon!" Australia Did It co-developer and game designer Rami Ismail said the game was originally submitted on October 20, and a minor controller issue caused it to fail. That bug was fixed the same day, but since then, Ismail and Aesthecian Labs have been stuck waiting for Steam approval. "We've been in the queue again ever since, and have followed up with Valve several times to no result," Rami explained in an email to GameSpot. "The issue was that our in-game feedback functionality does not allow you to send feedback--from a keyboard text input--via controller. I'm used to this kind of hold-and-wait pattern on console, but not really on Steam. 10-14 days pre-launch is usually enough to fail twice over, and usually you only get failed on serious issues." With reviews for Australia Did It already out, and the game on plenty of wishlists, not having it ready for its scheduled launch isn't doing it any favors. "Pre-emptively delaying the launch would've hurt, as did not doing so," Ismail…

title: Minerva Rising is a Frostpunk-meets-Silo underground city builder in which rebel citizens can hack your camera
description: Minerva Rising is a post-apocalyptic city builder in which your city extends deep underground, divided into levels with their own resources, industries, and communities. You are an artificial intelligence with overall control, but watch out: if you alienate the population of any particular level by, say, forgetting to supply them with oxygen, subversives may rise up and cut your feed, blinding you to their activities. I'm keen to know whether it's possible for every level to lose faith in you and hack your cameras, reducing the game to a pile of "SIGNAL NOT FOUND" messages. I'm also imagining turning the feeds back on and discovering that everybody is having a massive orgy. Stupid sexy vault dwellers! You'll go forth and multiply when Deep Thought tells you to, and not a second before. Read more

title: Honkai Star Rail’s First Playable Aeon Isn’t A Damage God, And That’s A Good Thing
description: The Aeons of Honkai Star Rail have always been far beyond ordinary mortals. They are conceptual deities whose actions have the potential to reshape entire galaxies--so putting one into a player's four-person team was always going to be a huge design challenge for the HoYoverse team. Ahead of the game's Version 4.7 update, we spoke to lead game designer Chengan An about why Aha, The Aeon of Elation, was chosen as the game's first playable Aeon. According to Chengan, the decision to bring Aha into the fold came down to their uniquely human disposition, as well as the development team's unwillingness to break the game's battle rules. Aha is meant to focus on collaborative synergy rather than racking up extreme damage numbers. Chengan also noted that Aha's personality is what makes them the most logical Aeon to bring to the battlefield at this point in the game's life cycle. "The game's system is based on the concept of Paths. For Aeons, they are quite abstract concepts for most of the people in the world, but Aha is the most human-like one." Chengan continued: "I think our [game's] battle is way too tiny for Aeons to initiate a war. For Aha, we picked some of the most important factors to bring into the combat design. We certainly don't want them to destroy the battle with the power of an Aeon, and that kind of design does not fit Aha's personality as an Aeon of Elation." HoYoverse viewed the Path of Elation as a foundation for Aha, one that's been built up over months of prior updates. "For the Path of Elation, we do not intend to simply bring a character with super-strong skills to overcome all the existing characters when we have already designed so many previous Paths. We aim to bring the Aeon of Elation to interact with our other characters, and that's why we have already presented so many characters that can interact with Aha. We think this kind of design can bring a fresh experience to our players when they see such an Aeon," Chengan explained. Chengan…

title: Best Loadouts In Call Of Duty: Warzone For MW4 Season 1
description: Modern Warfare 4 has integrated with Warzone for Season 1, adding MW4’s full weapon pool, attachments, and other new gear into battle royale. This means you'll want to update your loadouts for this new season. Our guide will recommend some of the best weapon builds for Warzone in Season 1 of Modern Warfare 4, as well as discuss some of the major changes to weapon customization this year. For best perks, make sure to check out our MW4 Warzone Season 1 perk guide. Weapon customization changes in Warzone for MW4 Gunsmith changes Call of Duty’s Gunsmith feature returns. This customization system lets you create five-attachment builds for Warzone. Guns from the older CoD's are still available to use as "Legacy" weapons, but you can no longer customize them in the Gunsmith. You can only customize MW4 guns. You can choose up to five standard attachments for your weapon build, and you can also include the gun's unique Apex attachment as a sixth optional attachment. Vel 46 Apex attachment Apex attachments are special add-ons you can unlock for each gun in MW4, which will drastically change how the weapon is used. Apex attachments are similar to the weapon conversion kits found in the recent Call of Duty games, but in Modern Warfare 4 they don’t cost one of your attachment slots. Apex attachments aren’t unlocked until you’ve reached the maximum weapon level for a specific gun. Some of these attachments are a bit wacky and aren’t practical add-ons, but others will offer viable bonuses to your weapon. Weapon augments Lootable weapon augments in-match Outside of the Gunsmith customization for your create-a-class weapons, it's also worth noting that you'll have an additional weapon augmentation you can find and apply during your match. Modern Warfare 4 adds brand-new weapon augments as a new way to upgrade your weapon with significant bonuses.
